title: Customs Amendment Bill, 2023
text:
CUSTOMS (AMENDMENT) BILL, 2023
library I

MEMORANDUM

The object of the Bill is to amend the First Schedule to the Customs
Act 2015, (Act 891) to add four hundred and thirty-one tariff lines to the
Customs Tariff and to provide a waiver for the importation of raw
materials for the manufacture of sanitary towels.

. The World Customs Organisation, an international body made up
of representatives of one hundred and eighty-three customs
administrations worldwide, undertakes a general revie'w of the
Harmonised Commodity Description and Coding System, also known
as the Harmonised System, every five years. The Harmonised System is
a product nomenclature developed by the World Customs Organisation
that serves as a basis for tariff schedules for more than two hundred
countries and economies worldwide.

..The key factors driving the review of the 2022 Harmonised System
include advances in technology, new product streams, changing trade
patterns, environmental consideration, health and safety and the fight
against terrorism.

The Economic Community of West African States Commission has
adopted the 2022 edition of the Harmonised System Code developed by
the World. Customs Organisation. To give proper definition and simplify
•commodity description and classification codes, the World Customs
Organisation has subdivided some of the tariff headings, and re-aligned
some chapters. This has r.esulted in amendment of a wide variety of
commodity codes, hence, the introduction of four hundred and thirty-one
tariff lines in the 2022 Economic Community of West' African States
Common External Tariff.

To strengthen regional economic integration within the Economic
Community of West African States sub-region, Ghana has complied with
the 2022 Economic Community of West African States Common
External Tariff. This has culminated in the creation of four hundred
and thirty-one tariff lines, which cover a wide range of goods in
conformity with the 2022 edition of the Harmonised System.

CUSTOMS (AMENDMENT) BILL, 2023

The Bill therefore seeks to amend the Customs Act, 2015 (Act 891)
to enable the country to adopt and implement th'e 2022 Economic
Community of West African States Common External Tariff, The
proposed amendment will add the new four hundred and thirty-one tariff
lines to the Customs Tariff and align the Value Added Tax and Excise
Duty rates with the respective tariff lines. The proposed amendment is
also expected to improve the customs classification and provide accurate
international trade statistics, and strengthen the economic integration of
the country with neighbours within the Economic Community of West
African States sub-region.

Finally, as part of the social contract and in response to appeals made
to Government to help reduce the cost of basic hygiene products and to
support production of sanitary towels to meet local’ demands, the Bill
seeks to provide an import duty exemption on raw materials for the
manufacture of the product. The waiver is estimated to cost
approximately six million Ghana Cedis.

The Bill consists of one clause which amends the First Schedule to
Act 891 to include the’new four hundred and thirty-one tariff lines with
their respective Common External-Tariffs. The clause also exempts raw
materials not locally available for the manufacture of sanitary towels from
the payment of import duty.
